title: To the Lighthouse
author: Virginia Woolf
summary: A family and their guests spend a summer holiday in a house by the sea, where a small trip to a lighthouse is promised and then put off. A decade later, changed by loss, some of them return.
readIf: you want a short, beautifully written study of family, memory and how time quietly rearranges people.
skipIf: you want chapters of action or dialogue, since much of it unfolds inside people's heads.

pairings.reason: The same author's more accessible novel, with a similar fluid voice and a London setting instead of the sea.
Reflective and elegiac, with a similar sense of lives measured by what was never said aloud.
Continues the thread of Woolf-style interior writing in a modern, more structured novel.
